unpeated-malt.summary: Speyside malts generally gain depth and sherry integration with age statements while losing some fresh fruit.

stages.label: Young (10–12)
stages.effect: Bright orchard fruit, honey and light vanilla; the barrel is a supporting player.

stages.label: Developing (15–18)
stages.effect: Dried fruit deepens, oak spice builds and the texture gains weight.

stages.label: Mature (21+)
stages.effect: Walnut, polished oak and marmalade; fresh fruit recedes into the background.

unpeated-malt.vintage: Cask type matters more than a couple of years' difference: first-fill sherry at 12 can taste older than refill at 18.

sherry-malt.summary: Sherry-cask Speyside malts generally deepen with age statements while fresh fruit recedes.

stages.label: Young (10–12)
stages.effect: Fresh dried fruit, bright sherry sweetness and lively oak spice.

stages.label: Developing (15–18)
stages.effect: Walnut, polished oak and darker fruit; the sherry integrates fully.

stages.label: Mature (21+)
stages.effect: Antique oak, marmalade and savoury depth; sweetness turns dignified.

sherry-malt.vintage: Cask type matters more than a couple of years: first-fill sherry at 12 can taste older than refill at 18.

heavily-peated-malt.summary: Peat slowly mellows with age while oak sweetness rises to meet it.

stages.label: Young (10)
stages.effect: Raw, aggressive smoke and brine; the peat is the whole story.

stages.label: Developing (16)
stages.effect: Smoke integrates with sherry or oak sweetness into a rounder whole.

stages.label: Mature (25+)
stages.effect: Peat softens to embers; dried fruit and polished oak lead.

heavily-peated-malt.vintage: High-peat bottlings vary batch to batch even at the same age statement.
